A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same score-Jacobian Riemannian metric research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data, image-interpolation, and video-frame-interpolation experiments, plus prompt-adjustment ablations and spectral analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original interpolation experiments and adds guidance-correction, distillation, checkpoint-robustness, and sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The metric G = J^T J and interpolation optimization are retained. Section 3.2 adds a distinct guidance-correction procedure: regularizing the guidance perturbation using the metric, approximately solving the resulting linear system with one conjugate-gradient step and finite-difference products, and applying correction to the distillation teacher.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates MorphBench metamorphosis, explicitly excluded in v1 because of its global shape changes. It also adds text-conditioned generation evaluated on MS-COCO 2014 validation prompts and distillation training on Conceptual 12M. The earlier synthetic, face-image, and video interpolation coverage remains.

E2.justification: The previously cited but unevaluated FIM-based metric of Azeglio and Bernardo becomes a comparator in image interpolation, video interpolation, and the prompt-adjustment ablation. New generation experiments evaluate CFG and CFG++, while distillation compares corrected and ordinary CFG teachers. The original five interpolation baselines remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include 30,000-image generation evaluated with FID and CLIP Score, four-step distilled-model evaluation, and interpolation using Stable Diffusion v2.0-base. Spectral analysis expands from one endpoint to all sampled CelebA-HQ images. Synthetic-step reporting also changes inconsistently: v2 Section 4.1 says training uses 50 steps, whereas Appendix D.1 specifies 1,000 training and 50 generation steps; an actual training change is therefore unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's prompt-adjustment ablation and qualitative noise-level study, v2 adds checkpoint-robustness experiments, quantitative noise-level sweeps for image and video interpolation, and guidance-weight and conjugate-gradient-iteration ablations. It also extends the prompt-adjustment comparison to the FIM-based metric and replaces the single-image spectral example with dataset-level analysis.

E5.justification: v1 reports no significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty analysis. v2 introduces one-sided exact binomial tests for interpolation comparisons, five matched-seed distillation runs with a reported significance result, and median, interquartile, and minimum–maximum spectral bands. These are newly reported practices; they do not establish additional runs of the retained interpolation experiments.

E6.justification: Previously reported interpolation numbers are retained, including the method's MB(A) FID of 27.44 and DAVIS MSE of 8.777 × 10^-3. v2 adds metamorphosis results, FIM-based comparator scores, different-checkpoint results, guidance and distillation outcomes, and sensitivity results. For example, new Table 5 reports distilled-model FID of 16.98 versus 17.91 for CFG; this is a new comparison, not a v1-to-v2 performance gain.

T1.justification: The original metric and spectral argument underlying Proposition 1 remain. v2 adds the guidance-correction variational formulation and its approximate linear-system derivation in Equations 4–5, with assumptions about neighboring-time geometry and Jacobian symmetry. It also develops the rank-one limitation of the FIM-based metric and explains why using the score Jacobian directly can yield an indefinite metric.

C1.justification: v1's central validation concerns manifold-aware interpolation. v2 broadens the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to claim complementary validation of global geometry through interpolation and local geometry through guidance correction. It additionally claims improved generation quality without reduced text alignment and transfer of that benefit to distilled models without extra student inference cost.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about interpolation metrics failing to reflect visual quality at low noise levels and explicitly frames video interpolation as a geometry proxy. It explains guidance-weight robustness and deterioration from accumulated approximation errors over additional solver iterations. It also identifies evaluation on newer architectures as unfinished work and expands the interpretation of the FIM-based comparator's limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds complete MorphBench prompt tables, FID sample counts, guidance implementation settings, and detailed LCM/LoRA training parameters. Hardware reporting changes from all experiments using an A100 to separate A6000, A100, and H200 assignments. Conversely, v1's statement that source code is attached as supplementary material disappears; the PDFs do not establish whether actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around guidance, contrasting its geometric correction with CFG++ and TCFG and adding guidance and distillation literature. It develops the distinction between its full Jacobian spectrum and the previously cited FIM-based metric's rank-one score direction. Related work is also reorganized into an explicit taxonomy of interpolation approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around global and local geometric validation. The main-text preliminaries move into Appendix A, the method gains separate metric and algorithm subsections, and the appendices are reorganized. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds geometric illustrations, algorithm boxes, guidance examples, prompt tables, and quantitative ablation plots. Table 2 is restructured into two metric blocks. Earlier video examples from v1 Figures 4 and 6 are consolidated into v2 Figure 7, while the spectral display is redesigned with distribution bands. Other interpolation examples are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central geometric argument by testing previously excluded metamorphosis cases, evaluating the FIM-based competitor, expanding spectral evidence beyond one image, and adding statistical and sensitivity analyses. The guidance experiments provide evidence beyond interpolation, while the new ablations expose metric and solver limitations. These gains outweigh the removed code-attachment statement and the conflicting synthetic-data training-step descriptions, which remain documentation weaknesses.
